proposals.before: He asked to treat him as a honored guest.
proposals.after: He asked to treat him as an honored guest.
proposals.reason: Clear grammar error: the article before honored must be an, not a.

proposals.before: Qin Hui's peace talk exiled loyal men and drained the realm's spirit.
proposals.after: When Qin Hui preached perverse talk to thwart them, loyal ministers and righteous men were cast out to die in the south, and the realm's spirit went slack.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents exile via peace talk and omits obstructive perverse counsel and death of the loyal in the south.

proposals.before: Whispers called you vain for glory; even the throne could not silence them, and you bore it seventeen years more.
proposals.after: Men then murmured against you in secret, saying you loved merit and ignored later trouble; even Your Majesty with exalted power could not prevail alone, and bore it in silence until now—another seventeen years.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents the throne silencing critics and drops loving merit without regard for later trouble.

proposals.before: At Bi, Luan Shu said, "Since Chu took Yong, its lord daily warned the people: 'Ah!
proposals.after: At the battle of Bi between Jin and Chu, Luan Shu said, "Since Chu took Yong, its lord daily warned the people: 'Ah!
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 晉、楚之戰, leaving only 'At Bi' and obscuring which states fought.

proposals.before: They eroded the state; even Zhang Dexiang and Chen Zhizhong could only slow the ruin.
proposals.after: Not only did they not aid the state's momentum, they further pared it away; though Zhang Dexiang and Chen Zhizhong in small part blocked them, how could the reformers not become discouraged themselves!
proposals.reason: Chinese 微 modifies the degree of obstruction by Zhang and Chen, and 自沮 refers to the reformers' self-discouragement; the idiomatic version invents 'slow the ruin' and loses the rhetorical question.

proposals.before: They missed that the state thrived on divided power, light counties, and heavy center—slow but sure.
proposals.after: They did not know that the court's founding momentum suffered precisely from civil forms being too dense, powers too divided, commanderies too light below and too petty to rely on, and troops and wealth too concentrated above and too heavy and slow to mobilize.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English reverses the sense of 正患: the text names over-dense civil forms, over-divided powers, overly light commanderies, and overly concentrated troops and wealth as the disease, not as virtues the state thrived on.

proposals.before: When Song took the Mandate, the Qian house entered the capital and yielded the land.
proposals.after: When our Song received the Mandate, Di Jin brought his whole house to the capital and himself offered the soil.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits personal subject 禘盡 present in Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: Two centuries on it was Three Kingdoms ground; Zhuge Liang gathered Jing-Chu men and Shu lived;
proposals.after: Two hundred years more it became the three states' contested ground; Zhuge Liang from here rose to aid the First Lord; Jing-Chu scholars followed like clouds, and the Han house relied on this to survive again in Shu;
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops 先主 whom Zhuge Liang aided.

proposals.before: Your Majesty resolutely moved the capital to Jianye; the hundred offices all followed from scratch; military and state ritual all followed simplicity; he also made a traveling palace at Wuchang to show intent not to dwell at ease.
proposals.after: Your Majesty resolutely moved the capital to Jianye; the hundred offices all followed from scratch; military and state ritual all followed simplicity; Your Majesty also made a traveling palace at Wuchang to show intent not to dwell at ease.
proposals.reason: Pronoun 'he' wrongly shifts continuing subject 陛下.

proposals.before: Between xinmao and renchen he first withdrew to exhaust Heaven-and-Earth's creating beginning, examine past and present change, to push to the utmost the ways of emperor, king, hegemon, and lord, and obtain Han, Wei, Jin, and Tang's causes of length and shortness; the border of Heaven and man is bright and can be examined and known.
proposals.after: Between xinmao and renchen I first withdrew to exhaust Heaven-and-Earth's creating beginning, examine past and present change, to push to the utmost the ways of emperor, king, hegemon, and lord, and obtain Han, Wei, Jin, and Tang's causes of length and shortness; the border of Heaven and man is bright and can be examined and known.
proposals.reason: Memorial first-person subject mistranslated as 'he'.

proposals.before: He first understood that today's Ruists who think they have the learning of rectifying heart and sincere intent are all men numb with wind paralysis who do not know pain or itch.
proposals.after: I first understood that today's Ruists who think they have the learning of rectifying heart and sincere intent are all men numb with wind paralysis who do not know pain or itch.
proposals.reason: Continues memorial speaker as 'he'.

proposals.before: Your Majesty received him but did not charge him with affairs—your subject therefore admires Your Majesty's benevolence.
proposals.after: Your Majesty received me but did not charge me with affairs—your subject therefore admires Your Majesty's benevolence.
proposals.reason: Object of 接之 is the memorialist.

proposals.before: He further understood that today's talented ministers who think they have rich-state strong-army methods are all men mad and shouting wildly.
proposals.after: I further understood that today's talented ministers who think they have rich-state strong-army methods are all men mad and shouting wildly.
proposals.reason: Memorial first person rendered as 'he'.

proposals.before: I foolishly think that the instruments by which the state has maintained itself are now exhausted, yet the great plan by which Emperor Yizu laid out the realm can still be relied upon for the long term. If we trace his intention back to its source and adapt it, recovery will not be difficult.
proposals.after: I foolishly think that the instruments by which the state has maintained itself are now exhausted, yet the great plan by which Emperor Taizu laid out the realm can still be relied upon for the long term. If we trace his intention back to its source and adapt it, recovery will not be difficult.
proposals.reason: 藝祖皇帝 is Song Taizu; 'Emperor Yizu' invents a misleading English form inconsistent with the idiomatic Taizu.

proposals.before: Vice Minister He Dan had once been an examination official and demoted Liang; Liang was discontent and several times spoke insulting Dan; Dan heard and resented him, and at once forwarded the report.
proposals.after: Vice Minister He Dan had once been an examination official and failed Liang; Liang was discontent and several times spoke insulting Dan; Dan heard and resented him, and at once forwarded the report.
proposals.reason: In the examination setting 黜亮 means he failed Liang as a candidate, not that he demoted him from office.

proposals.before: Once officials heard of it, he had the boy beaten with the cudgel until the lad died and revived several times, but the servant still refused to admit guilt.
proposals.after: When the matter was reported to the authorities, the servant was flogged with the bamboo until he died and revived several times, yet still would not confess.
proposals.reason: The Chinese reports the servant being flogged after the matter reached the authorities; idiomatic 'he had the boy beaten' invents a false agent.

proposals.before: Vice Minister Zheng Runan read the lone confession and exclaimed, 'Here is a wonder of the age.
proposals.after: Vice Minister Zheng Ruxie read the lone confession and exclaimed, 'Here is a wonder of the age.
proposals.reason: 鄭汝諧 is Zheng Ruxie (Rúxié); Runan is an incorrect romanization of 汝諧.

proposals.before: The vice minister Zheng Runan, reading the solitary testimony, was greatly astonished and said: 'This is a rare talent of the realm.
proposals.after: The vice minister Zheng Ruxie, reading the solitary testimony, was greatly astonished and said: 'This is a rare talent of the realm.
proposals.reason: 鄭汝諧 is Zheng Ruxie (Rúxié); Runan misreads the given name 汝諧.

proposals.before: When war was launched in the Kaixi era and the Jin watched the San Pass with urgency, Daochuan, on orders from the various offices to plan affairs, heard on the road that Wu Xi had rebelled; grief and rage showed in his face.
proposals.after: When war was launched in the Kaixi era and the Jin watched the San Pass with urgency, Daochuan, on orders from the various offices to plan affairs, then heard that Wu Xi had rebelled; grief and rage showed in his face.
proposals.reason: Chinese 道聞 continues 道傳 as subject (or equals 適聞), not hearing while traveling; literal invents 'on the road'.

proposals.before: Early in Jiading he became academy erudite, then court-of-sacrifices erudite and tutor in the Prince of Qi's school.
proposals.after: Early in Jiading he became academy erudite, then court-of-sacrifices erudite and tutor in the Prince of Yi's school.
proposals.reason: 沂王 is Prince of Yi (Yí), not Qi (齊).

proposals.before: At the beginning of the Jiading era he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then promoted to Erudite of the Court of Sacrifices while also instructing the primary school of the Prince of Qi's residence.
proposals.after: At the beginning of the Jiading era he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then promoted to Erudite of the Court of Sacrifices while also instructing the primary school of the Prince of Yi's residence.
proposals.reason: Same 沂/Qi mistranslation as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: As acting prefect of Xuan he enforced Zhu Xi's community granaries; Shangrao, Xin'an, Nanchang, and neighboring circuits followed suit and the people gained.
proposals.after: As acting prefect of Xuan he enforced Zhu Xi's community granaries; Shangrao, Xin'an, Nankang, and neighboring circuits followed suit and the people gained.
proposals.reason: 南康 is Nankang, not Nanchang (南昌).

proposals.before: Acting as magistrate of Xuanzhou, he implemented Zhu Xi's community granary law; Shangrao, Xin'an, Nanchang, and other prefectures responded as one, and the people profited.
proposals.after: Acting as magistrate of Xuanzhou, he implemented Zhu Xi's community granary law; Shangrao, Xin'an, Nankang, and other prefectures responded as one, and the people profited.
proposals.reason: Same 南康/Nanchang error as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: He had three sons—Dake, Dangke, and Xiankhe.
proposals.after: He had three sons—Dake, Dangke, and Xianke.
proposals.reason: 獻可 romanizes as Xianke; Xiankhe is a corrupted spelling.

proposals.before: Three sons: Dake, Dangke, and Xiankhe.
proposals.after: Three sons: Dake, Dangke, and Xianke.
proposals.reason: Same Xiankhe/Xianke corruption as in the idiomatic field.

decisions.reason: 上客 is 'honored guest'; English 'a honored' is an article error, and 'an honored' is the required grammatical fix.
Chinese 倡邪議以沮之 and 斥死南方 name perverse counsel thwarting resistance and loyal men cast out to die in the south; 'peace talk exiled' invents exile via peacemaking and drops those elements.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 倡邪議以沮之，忠臣義士斥死南方

decisions.reason: Chinese 喜功名而不恤後患 and 不能以崇高之勢而獨勝之 are loving merit without regard for later trouble and inability to prevail alone; 'throne could not silence them' invents silencing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 喜功名而不恤後患，雖陛下亦不能以崇高之勢而獨勝之

decisions.reason: 晉、楚之戰於邲 names Jin and Chu fighting at Bi; bare 'At Bi' omits which states fought, and the repair restores that.
微章得象、陳執中以排沮 and 安得而不自沮哉 mark slight obstruction and the reformers' self-discouragement in a rhetorical question; 'slow the ruin' invents a different outcome.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雖微章得象、陳執中以排沮其事，亦安得而不自沮哉

decisions.reason: 正患文為之太密，事權之太分 names those conditions as the disease; 'thrived on divided power…slow but sure' reverses 正患 into a virtue.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 正患文為之太密，事權之太分，郡縣太輕於下

decisions.after: When our Song received the Mandate, Chu brought his whole house to the capital and himself offered the soil.
decisions.reason: Chapter 禘盡 is a corrupt personal-name reading; Wikisource has 俶盡, i.e. Qian Chu entirely bringing his house. Proposed 'Di Jin' invents a false name, while bare 'Qian house' still omits the personal subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 俶盡以其家入京師，而自獻其土

decisions.reason: 諸葛亮由此起輔先主 keeps 先主 as the one Zhuge Liang aided; the before text drops that referent.
又作行宮 continues 陛下 as subject; 'he also made' wrongly shifts the agent away from Your Majesty.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 陛下慨然移都建業……又作行宮於武昌

decisions.reason: Context 臣 and the memorial voice make the subject first person; 'he first withdrew' misattributes the speaker.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 始退而窮天地造化之初

decisions.reason: 始悟 continues the memorialist's first-person realization; 'He first understood' misattributes it.
接之 points to the memorialist (臣); 'received him' invents a third-person object.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 陛下接之而不任以事，臣於是服陛下之仁

decisions.reason: 又悟 continues the same first-person memorial insight; 'He further understood' is the wrong person.
藝祖皇帝 is Song Taizu's conventional epithet; 'Emperor Yizu' invents a misleading English name against that usage.
考試官，黜亮 in an examination setting means failing the candidate; 'demoted' invents removal from office.
聞於官，笞榜僮 is a passive report that the servant was flogged; 'he had the boy beaten' invents an unauthorized agent.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 聞於官，笞榜僮，死而復甦者數，不服

decisions.reason: 鄭汝諧 romanizes as Zheng Ruxie (汝諧 Rúxié); Runan misreads 諧.
Same 鄭汝諧; literal Runan is the same wrong given-name reading, and Ruxie restores it.
道聞 after 道傳以諸司檄計事 continues Daochuan as subject (or 適聞 'then heard'); 'heard on the road' invents travel from 道.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 道傳以諸司檄計事，道聞吳曦反

decisions.reason: 沂王 is Prince of Yi (Yí); Qi would be 齊, so Prince of Qi is a wrong toponymic title.
Same 沂王; literal Prince of Qi repeats the 沂/齊 confusion, and Prince of Yi matches the graph.
南康 is Nankang; Nanchang is 南昌, so the before text substitutes the wrong prefecture.
Same 南康; literal Nanchang is the same wrong place-name, and Nankang restores it.
獻可 is Xianke; Xiankhe is a corrupted spelling of the same name.
Same 獻可; literal Xiankhe is the same corruption, and Xianke is the correct romanization.

Accepted r0017 restores personal name Zheng Ruxie for 鄭汝諧; Runan was translation-only error.
Accepted r0020 restores Prince of Yi for 沂王; Qi would be 齊 and was a translation error.
